headline: Makers of power-management, display-driver and microcontroller chips are weighing price rises of at least 5% as TSMC is reported to be raising its chip-making fees again from January.
score_reason: Kept at the pool level: new knock-on detail beyond the 5 Oct TSMC story, but a research-firm report with TSMC's rises still unconfirmed.
importance_line: If the rises go through, makers of electronics could pay more early next year for chips that manage power, drive screens and run simple controls, but the TSMC rises are unconfirmed reports and the figures differ from our 5 Oct report.
summary: Maeil Business Newspaper, a Korean daily, reports, citing the research firm TrendForce, that makers of power-management, display-driver and microcontroller chips are weighing price rises of 5% to double digits between the end of 2026 and early 2027 to cover higher chip-making costs. New since our 5 Oct report of a further TSMC price rise, the paper says, citing unnamed reports, that TSMC, the world's largest contract chipmaker, is expected to raise prices again from January, with a rise of about 3% to 10% under discussion for older "mature" processes, and has reportedly decided on a further 6% to 8% for 2-nanometer wafers in the first quarter; those figures differ from the 3% to 6% in the earlier report.
notes: Follows up C08-07 of the 5 Oct edition (TSMC price rise, DigiTimes via Technetbooks). Credit chain: Maeil relays TrendForce; TrendForce's own page not found. TSMC figures are 'reportedly', unnamed source. 2-nanometer figure (6% to 8%) differs from the 3% to 6% for advanced wafers in the earlier report.
